title: Explicit v.s. Implicit Memory: Exploring Multi-hop Complex Reasoning Over Personalized Information

problem.claim: Personalized agents need to perform multi-hop reasoning over large amounts of user information.

gap.claim: Existing memory-based personalization studies typically address preference alignment and simple question-answering rather than complex multi-hop reasoning.

contributions.claim: The authors propose the multi-hop personalized reasoning task for evaluating memory mechanisms on multi-hop reasoning over personalized information.
The authors define the task and construct a dataset with a unified evaluation framework.
The authors explore hybrid explicit and implicit memory approaches and propose HybridMem to address their limitations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report comprehensive experiments implementing various explicit and implicit memory methods.
The authors report evaluating performance from multiple perspectives and analyzing the strengths and weaknesses of the methods.
The authors report that extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of HybridMem.

narrative_sequence.summary: Memory is presented as important for personalization in language-model-based agents.

Prior personalization studies are described as focusing mainly on preference alignment and simple question-answering, while real-world complex tasks require multi-hop reasoning over substantial user information.
The authors introduce a multi-hop personalized reasoning task and provide a dataset and unified evaluation framework.
They implement explicit and implicit memory methods and evaluate them from multiple perspectives.
They investigate hybrid memory, propose HybridMem, report its effectiveness, and release the project.

source_observation.claim: The abstract frames personalization research as insufficient when tasks require multi-hop reasoning over large amounts of user information.

interpretation.claim: Memory evaluation for personalized agents should include complex reasoning workloads rather than only preference alignment and simple question-answering.

application.claim: Use multi-hop personalized reasoning as an evaluation scenario for comparing memory mechanisms.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this evaluation scenario generalizes beyond the supplied task or dataset.

source_observation.claim: The authors examine explicit, implicit, and hybrid memory approaches and report proposing HybridMem to address limitations of the separate paradigms.

interpretation.claim: Combining complementary memory paradigms may be a useful direction when individual mechanisms have different strengths and weaknesses.

application.claim: Compare individual memory mechanisms with hybrid combinations under a common evaluation framework.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which limitations are addressed or which hybrid components produce the reported effectiveness.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset size, composition, or task examples.
The abstract does not report quantitative results, baselines, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not describe the implementation or mechanism of HybridMem.
The abstract does not specify the experimental conditions or limitations of the reported findings.
